描述_ZN: White porcelain and blue-and-white porcelain fired in southern China during the late Ming to late Ming periods and painted with red, blue, and green overglaze enameling are called gosu-aka-e in Japan. There are quite a few examples of Go-su-aka-e vessels in the history of Japan, especially those with a kylin design in the center of the front, as shown in this example. Recently, excavations in China have revealed that the kiln in Fujian Province was one of the production sites.
